seoPage.title: Fast Charging vs Slow Charging — What Indian Owners Need | EVSavari
seoPage.metaDescription: Fast Charging vs Slow Charging — What Indian Owners Need — practical charging guidance for Indian buyers.
seoPage.intro: Fast DC and slow AC solve different problems. This guide helps you choose habits that match your parking, commute, and occasional highway trips — without overbuilding home infrastructure.

editorialSections.title: Definitions without jargon overload
paragraphs: Slow charging usually means AC overnight or during work hours. Fast charging means DC sessions at public stations for quicker top-ups.

editorialSections.title: Real-world practicality
bullets: City commute under ~40–50 km/day: AC often sufficient if you park 6–8 hours.
Monthly highway leg: plan DC stops using realistic range, not brochure peaks.
Apartment without dedicated point: treat public AC/DC as backup — start RWA talks early.

editorialSections.title: Charging safety notes
bullets: Use certified install for home AC — avoid ad-hoc extension boards.
In rain, use equipment rated for outdoor use — follow OEM guidance.

misconceptions.myth: Maximum DC kW is all that matters
misconceptions.reality: On-board limits and battery temperature still cap speed.

misconceptions.myth: Home must match public DC speed
misconceptions.reality: Home AC is about convenience, not highway parity.

faq.question: How long does home AC take?
faq.answer: Depends on kW, battery size, and start level — think hours, not minutes.

faq.question: When is DC worth it?
faq.answer: Highway legs, urgent top-ups, or when home charging is unavailable.

faq.question: Will slow charging damage the battery?
faq.answer: AC overnight is a common, gentle pattern — follow OEM guidance.

faq.question: Apartment owners?
